what_it_does: This paper describes a ultra-high-speed communication link (212.5 gigabits per second) connecting AI chips together in a data center. The core problem: over the short distances on a circuit board, metal traces pick up noise and distort the signal severely—losing 50 decibels (about 100,000 times weaker). To recover the signal, the receiver uses a three-part strategy: (1) an ultra-sensitive analog amplifier that amplifies with minimal added noise, (2) advanced digital signal processing (DSP, like audio equalizer software) that removes the distortion mathematically, and (3) a decoder that picks the most likely signal pattern given the noisy evidence, similar to how spam filters guess the intended message.
